source.title: GenARM: Reward Guided Generation with Autoregressive Reward Model for Test-time Alignment
source.authors: Yuancheng Xu; Udari Madhushani Sehwag; Alec Koppel; Sicheng Zhu; Bang An; Furong Huang; Sumitra Ganesh

page_placements.theme: Decoding-, logit- or activation-level guidance of a frozen stronger model by smaller models (proxy-tuning, reward-guided decoding, steering vectors)

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Applies weak-to-strong guidance in a new setting: a smaller reward model guides frozen larger language models at test time. It reports outcomes for that method, but does not test the claim’s fine-tuning-on-weak-model-labels intervention or its PGR measure.
record.gate_note: The weak-to-strong results use a 7B reward model trained on UltraFeedback preference data to guide frozen Tulu2 SFT models; the paper does not state that the labels were produced by a weaker model. The reported gap is relative to separately DPO-fine-tuned models, not the claim’s weak-supervisor/strong-ceiling PGR. No rows are included for the paper’s general alignment comparisons unrelated to weak-to-strong guidance.
record.test_reason: The paper uses 'weak-to-strong' as a label for test-time guidance of frozen larger LLMs by a 7B reward model trained on human preference data (UltraFeedback, PKU-SafeRLHF). No strong model is fine-tuned on a weaker model's labels, and there is no weak-supervisor baseline or strong ceiling in the PGR sense. Its '70% gap recovered' is measured between the 70B SFT model and the 70B DPO model, a different quantity. It reports its own method's performance against other decoding methods, so this is T4 rather than T3.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that GenARM's autoregressive RM enables efficient test-time alignment: it beats test-time baselines and matches DPO. A 7B RM guides larger frozen LLMs, recovering >70% of the 70B SFT–DPO gap on AlpacaEval 2 vs Tulu2-7B, and supports multi-objective alignment. They frame this as an example of weak-to-strong generalization, but the paper does not test Burns et al.'s setup.
record.recipe_differences: The original claim concerns fine-tuning a strong model on labels from a weaker model and measuring PGR. This paper uses a smaller reward model trained on preference data to guide frozen models during generation; its reported gap comparison is against DPO-fine-tuned models.
record.method_sensitivity: The tested base-model scale varies across Tulu2-7B, Tulu2-13B, and Tulu2-70B while the reward model remains 7B. The multi-objective experiment varies reward coefficients.

fits_no_version.finding: A 7B autoregressive RM guiding frozen Tulu2 SFT models at test time improves AlpacaEval 2 win rates at 7B, 13B and 70B. At 70B it recovers >70% of the SFT-to-DPO gap against Tulu2-7B, and >60% LC / 50% raw against GPT-4.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small reward models can steer larger frozen LLMs at test time, recovering much of the gap to training-time alignment of the large model.

fits_no_version.finding: 7B helpfulness and harmlessness autoregressive RMs steer Alpaca-65B along a trade-off frontier.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small reward models provide multi-objective test-time guidance to larger frozen models.

record.code_released: not stated; project page listed as https://genarm.github.io
record.problems: For the weak-to-strong results, plotted values are not stated numerically in the text and uncertainty estimates are not reported. The 70B model is quantized. The reported gap comparison is not the specified weak-supervisor PGR.
record.rows_left_out: No direct weak-label fine-tuning or PGR results are reported. Other GenARM comparisons not specifically bearing on weak-to-strong guidance were not extracted.

untested.parts: No strong model fine-tuned on weak-model labels; no comparison with the weak supervisor.
No auxiliary confidence loss, supervisor ensembling or loss variants for weak-to-strong training.
Base-model scale varies under test-time guidance, but PGR dependence on supervisor or student size, task or representations is not measured.
No exploitation, distribution-shift or shared-error analysis.
The theory concerns reward-parametrisation expressiveness, not when a student must beat its supervisor.

missing.what: Gap recovery against GPT-4 as the reference: >60% LC and 50% raw win rate at 70B. Also BoN surpasses DPO-70B in LC win rate in that comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The term 'weak-to-strong' is borrowed. The supervision signal is human preference data passed through a smaller RM, not a weak model's labels used to fine-tune a strong model. Tranche changed from T3 to T4 because the paper reports its own method's performance versus baselines. The 70B models are GPTQ-quantized. Values are figure-only.

versions.untested_parts: Does not fine-tune a strong student on labels produced by a weaker model or compare that student with the weak supervisor.
Does not test auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling weak supervisors, or the specified loss variants for PGR.
Varies the size of the frozen base model while using a 7B reward model, but does not measure the specified fine-tuning PGR or its dependence on supervisor size, task, or representations.
Does not test exploitation of supervisor blind spots, distribution shift, or shared-error effects.
Its theory concerns reward-model expressiveness for controlled decoding, not conditions under which a student must beat its supervisor.
Experiments are on language models; no vision results.

relation.reason: Applies weak-to-strong guidance at test time without training a strong student on weak-model labels or measuring improvement over the weak supervisor.

tranche.reason: Uses smaller-model guidance as a tool and reports GenARM performance. Frozen-model decoding and SFT-to-DPO gap recovery do not test any listed claim version.

source_check.notes: All six rows describe the study's own method and fit no claim version; cannot_determine is appropriate. Appendix C.3 specifies GPTQ-quantized 70B SFT and DPO checkpoints and confirms the GPT-4 comparison's gap-recovery statements.
